Before you calculate an overcharge, define which invoices belong in the audit.

A clean starting population answers: which carriers, dates, freight modes, entities and existing credits are included?

If the scope keeps changing, the savings number becomes difficult to defend. A suspicious difference is not yet a realized recovery.

A freight audit starts with a denominator, not a dollar sign.

Before reviewing carrier charges, freeze the entities, carriers, freight modes, billing dates, currencies and exclusions. Reconcile prior disputes and credits so the same correction isn't claimed twice.

A potential billing difference is a question. A validated finding needs evidence. A recovered amount needs actual eligible funds or credits.

Before comparing a carrier's fuel charge with an online index, confirm the agreement governing that shipment, the effective surcharge table, the index/lookback period, eligible base charges and rounding.

No controlling source? Leave the issue unresolved—don't automatically take the cheaper number.

content.suggested_image_alt_text: RETALLY illustrative freight detention review: gate-in 08:30, gate-out 11:00, 150 minutes onsite, hypothetically 120 free minutes, and 30 minutes beyond free time. Not a real charge or customer result.

instagram.caption:
ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE — NOT A CUSTOMER RESULT.

A gate log says 08:30 in and 11:00 out: 150 minutes onsite.

If the signed terms hypothetically allow 120 free minutes starting at arrival, 30 minutes would remain beyond free time. If 90 minutes were billed, that is a 60-minute question—not an established overcharge.

Appointment rules, actual triggers, exceptions, minimum charges, corrections and credits may change the answer.

Save the calculation for your next detention review.

#RETALLY #DetentionCharges #FreightAudit

facebook.caption:
ILLUSTRATIVE DETENTION CASE — NOT A CUSTOMER RESULT.

Gate in: 08:30. Gate out: 11:00. Total onsite: 150 minutes.

Assume a signed contract hypothetically allows 120 free minutes from arrival and no exceptions. That leaves 30 minutes beyond free time. An invoice for 90 detention minutes warrants review of the extra 60.

The gate timestamps alone do not establish a carrier error. Verify the contractual trigger, appointment provisions, corrections and prior credits.

content.suggested_image_alt_text: RETALLY illustrative settlement ledger distinguishing approved claim, posted and usable credit, and possible reversal, with no invented dollar amounts or customer outcomes.

instagram.caption:
The carrier approved a freight credit. Is that money recovered?

Not necessarily.

Approval, posted credit, usable account offset, actual refund and later reversal are different events.

A good recovery report identifies which stage each amount reached and reconciles any reversal before describing net eligible funds.

Don't confuse estimated savings with cash. Save this finance-control distinction.

#RETALLY #FreightRecovery #FinanceControls

facebook.caption:
"Credit approved" is not the same as "money recovered."

An approved dispute may become a credit memo, later a usable account adjustment or a refund. It may also be reversed.

A reliable recovery ledger ties each event to the original finding and reports net eligible value actually received under the written engagement terms. No particular outcome is guaranteed.

content.suggested_image_alt_text: RETALLY freight data stewardship artwork: general questions and scope may be discussed openly, while invoices and private rate agreements require separately agreed secure record transfer. No customer data.

instagram.caption:
Do not send freight invoices, rate agreements, account numbers or bank details in social DMs.

Start with non-sensitive context: what freight modes, carriers and billing periods are under review?

Only after fit and scope are agreed should sensitive records be transferred through an approved secure route. An email draft or a DM is not evidence that RETALLY received a customer request.

Share this privacy reminder with your AP team.

#RETALLY #FreightAudit #DataStewardship

facebook.caption:
Social messages are for general questions—not confidential freight files.

A practical initial conversation can cover freight mode, carriers, rough billing periods and audit scope. Keep invoices, private contracts, account identifiers and payment details out of comments and DMs.

Confidential records require an agreed secure transfer route and appropriate authorization first.
